thread:
Maya R.: Heads up — saw 12 GPU pod preemptions in ap-southeast1 in the last 2h, mostly tiny-gang jobs. Evictions line up with warm-pool drain events.
Ryan: ugh, any recent scheduler changes pushed to that region?
Pooja: pushed a topology-weight tweak last night (rollout id: rot-2026-07). It should favor rack locality more.
Maya R.: alert spiked at 09:14 UTC, pods went pending then re-scheduled to on-demand which bumped cost. Details: 
```
Alert: gpu_eviction_rate > 5 / 15m
Affected AZs: ap-southeast1-a/b
Pods: tiny-gang-* (preempted)
```
infra-bot: [ALERT] 1718001200 - GPU Preemptions (ap-southeast1) - Rate: 8/15m - Incident page: https://redwood/ops/INC-3931
Sam K.: do we have logs showing warm-pool lifecycle? could be warm-pool grace timing too short so new pods see no warm slot and get preempted.
Maya R.: grabbing logs now. quick snippet of scheduler events: 
```
Events:
  - Pod tiny-gang-5 failed to bind: no available slot -> queued
  - WarmPool drain started for pool-az-a, draining 4 slots (grace=30s)
  - Pod tiny-gang-5 scheduled on on-demand-node-12 -> preempted later
```
Pooja: we did reduce warm-pool grace from 60s -> 30s to increase binpack density last week. Might be too aggressive for tiny-gang bursty patterns.
Ryan: that would explain it. When warm-pool drains while a gang is forming, some pods get forced onto on-demand and cause preempts.
Li W.: proposed quick fix: revert warm-pool grace to 60s for ap-southeast1 only, add a canary label and monitor preempt rate for 30m. Command: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch config warmpool-ap-southeast1 -p '{"spec":{"graceSeconds":60}}' --type=merge
```
Sam K.: also suggest adding a taint-toleration window for tiny-gang workloads so they wait for warm slots for X seconds instead of falling back immediately. e.g., toleration: "wait-for-warm: 30s" (scheduler-side feature flag).
Pooja: we can toggle feature-flag in region: 
```
api call: POST /v1/flags/regions/ap-southeast1/scheduler.wait_for_warm -> true
```
Maya R.: timeline: can we patch warm-pool grace in 10m? If revert reduces preempts, we keep and plan follow-up telemetry.
Ryan: +1. I'll stand by to roll and watch cost dashboards.
Pooja: will patch and roll canary to az-a only first. Patch id: wp-revert-1718.
infra-bot: [DEPLOY] warmpool-config patched in ap-southeast1-a (user: Pooja) - rollout 10% -> 100% over 20m
Maya R.: after 12m, preempt rate down to 1/15m, small cost bump but much fewer spillovers. Good sign.
Sam K.: follow-up action items: 1) add small-pod affinity hints to tiny-gang job template, 2) add metric: warmpool-drain-overlaps-gang-start, 3) consider scheduler backoff rather than immediate fallback.
Li W.: I'll file the RFC for scheduler toleration semantics and a prod experiment for 2h warm-slot reservation for high-gang-ratio workloads.
Maya R.: thanks all. tagging @oncall to keep eyes for next 4h and file postmortem if we see regression. :thumbsup:
